analysis.title: Amneal Pharmaceuticals (AMRX): Management meeting frames FY27+ outlook
key_insights: GS hosted a dinner with AMRX's co-CEO, CFO, SVP Corporate Finance and Head of IR after a strong 3Q report and +70% YTD stock performance. The discussion centered on FY27+ growth.

Management expects growth in all three segments (generics, specialty, distribution) in FY27. The long-term earnings algorithm (HSD topline, LDD EBITDA, MDD EPS growth) is described as intact through FY30+.
Generics are expected to grow at a double-digit rate in FY27, driven by the base business, women's health patches, generic lanreotide and iohexol, among others.

Generic lanreotide was approved by the FDA in late September 2026. 3Q revenue was about $7mn, and management expects a multiple of that in 4Q. Targeted market share is 30% to 40% over time, potentially 30% by next year. The 120 mg prefilled syringe is about 90% of addressable volume.

Lanreotide 60 mg and 90 mg supplements are to be submitted in 4Q26, with launches expected in 2H27. A European decision is expected in 3Q27. Amneal keeps 100% of lanreotide profits because the product originated in Kashiv.
Management expects growth in lanreotide to moderate by FY28/29, but views the sales as durable with only modest erosion given the manufacturing complexity.

Women's health HRT transdermal patches: the Piscataway, NJ site expanded in 2026, with further capacity being added to address nationwide supply deficits. 3-year contracts are in place with major distributors/PBMs, and the company is working to extend them to 5 years. Management sees limited additional competitor entry before FY30.

bXolair (omalizumab biosimilar): US launch expected in 2H27, subject to patent settlement discussions. The FDA target action date is early 2027. AMRX expects to be the second biosimilar entrant after Celltrion, ahead of filers such as Teva. Expected volume is about 60% private label and 40% direct.

Denosumab biosimilar is expected to launch in mid-2027. Iohexol is the sole generic entrant, and AMRX now has approvals and filings for the remaining strengths and vials, allowing full-basket contracting with hospitals and imaging networks.

Specialty: Crexont (Parkinson's) is expected to grow more than 50% in FY27, with IP protection until 2038. Peak sales potential is $300mn to $500mn, and management points to the upper end of long-term guidance. Brekiya (migraine autoinjector) is expected to double in FY27, with peak sales above $100mn.
Teva's generic of Rytary was recently approved. AMRX has launched its own authorized generic, and management expects Crexont growth to offset Rytary erosion.

Long-term target: net revenue rises from $3.15bn-$3.25bn in 2026 to $4.3bn-$4.5bn by 2030, more than $1bn of incremental revenue. Biosimilars enabled by the Kashiv acquisition are the largest contributor, targeting a $234bn decade-long loss-of-exclusivity wave.

Management expects gross margin (about 46.5% in 2026) and operating margin to expand through FY30+ on mix shift to complex generics, biosimilars and specialty, despite higher absolute R&D spend. Leverage is targeted below 3.0x adjusted EBITDA by 2028.
Kashiv synergies: $400mn to $500mn of combined operational and tax synergies, including $60mn of recently awarded New Jersey tax credits. AMRX retains 100% of product economics.

Pfizer GLP-1 partnership: two dedicated facilities (drug substance and drug product) are on schedule for completion between late 2028 and 2029, and management expects a financial contribution in FY29+. Terms for the 18 international markets licensed to Amneal, including duration and co-commercialization, are being finalized, and an update is expected in the near term. Pfizer is evaluating a branded model in those markets. The facilities also give CDMO optionality.

GS rates AMRX Buy with a 12-month price target of $24 (raised from $21 on 29-Oct-26), based on 12x EV/EBITDA applied to NTM estimates 12 months out. Price was $21.39 at the 19 Nov 2026 close, implying 12.2% upside.

market_movers.rationale: GS reiterates Buy after a management dinner, citing growth across all segments in FY27 and an intact long-term earnings algorithm. The $24 target uses 12x EV/EBITDA on NTM estimates 12 months out.

earnings_insights: AMRX 3Q26 report described as strong. Third-quarter generic lanreotide revenue was about $7mn, and management expects a multiple of that in 4Q26.
GS estimates, EPS: $0.83 for FY25 (actual), $1.05 FY26E, $1.17 FY27E, $1.33 FY28E. Quarterly EPS: $0.30 for 6/26 (actual), $0.24 for 9/26E, $0.24 for 12/26E, $0.26 for 3/27E.
GS estimates, revenue: $3,018.8mn FY25, $3,145.1mn FY26E, $3,391.4mn FY27E, $3,660.3mn FY28E. EBITDA: $688.4mn FY25, $782.1mn FY26E, $839.8mn FY27E, $944.8mn FY28E.
Company 2026 net revenue target of $3.15bn-$3.25bn is management guidance. The 2030 target is $4.3bn-$4.5bn.
risk_factors: Higher-than-expected generic price erosion in the US, or failure to execute on new product launches such as biosimilars.
Commercial setbacks in the branded business, such as weaker growth for Crexont, Brekiya or Unithroid.
Clinical or regulatory setbacks, including negative readouts, development delays, or failure or delay of approvals.
Litigation, including settlement terms or an inability to launch products when expected because of patent litigation.
bXolair launch timing depends on the conclusion of patent settlement discussions.
vol_and_positioning: AMRX is up 70% YTD. GS lists 3m ADTV of $61.8mn and an M&A rank of 3 (low probability of becoming an acquisition target, 0%-15%).
